newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rival files complaint against D.Telekom.
newsitem.headline: Rival files complaint against D.Telekom.

text.p: O.Tel.O., the telecoms venture of utilities Veba AG and RWE AG, said on Monday it filed a complaint with the government against Deutsche Telekom AG, saying talks with the phone giant over interconnection had reached a dead-end.

Under German law the Post and Telecommunications Ministry, responsible for telecoms regulation until 1998, now has 10 weeks to set the terms by which O.Tel.O will be able to lease access to the network of monopoly Deutsche Telekom.
"Telekom wants to misuse its power in the market to prevent our reaching telephone customers with better service and lower prices," said O.Tel.O chairman Ulf Bohla in a statement.

He said the complaint against Telekom filed with the Post and Telecommunications Ministry on Monday was "directed against Telekom's refusal to grant O.Tel.O direct access to the lines of end customers.
"O.Tel.O expects that it will also come to regulatory complaints regarding other details of the interconnection negotiations," the statement said.

Because Deutsche Telekom as the former monopolist is the only phone company with access to virtually every home and business in Germany, its new rivals must lease its lines to gain access to customers.

Dubbed interconnection in industry jargon, these agreements form the cost basis for Telekom's rivals and without clarity over interconnection tariffs they cannot plan their networks or calculate their costs.
Most European Union countries, including Germany, will open their telecoms markets to full competition in January, 1998. Such interconnection agreements must be in place before then.
"Deutsche Telekom wants to force us to accept services that we neither need nor want and that make our offer to customers more expensive and less flexible," said Bohla.
"We are not seeking special treatment or a period of protection, but rather just fair terms for competition."
